text:
Anya Patel: Heads up — planning to add a compact GPU nodepool in us-west4 to serve low-latency compact-infer workloads. Need a quick preflight: quotas, subnet IPs, taints/labels, autoscaler min/max, and recommended instance SKU vs cost tradeoffs.
Kevin Chen: +1. What's target size / burst behavior? will this be preemptible-only or mixed?
Anya Patel: baseline 4 nodes, can burst to 12. Prefer a mixed spot + reserved approach if quota allows. Taint nodes so only inference pods land there.
Luca Marino: For us-west4 we have 18 free A10 GPUs quota-wise right now, but subnet IPs in that cluster's node-subnet are low — only ~30 IPs left, need /24 or secondary range bump.
SRE-OnCall: caution — autoscaler churn if max-min tight. Set min to 2 (or 1 if you can tolerate cold-warm) and max to 12. Use node pool with a dedicated taint: `redwood.com/gpu=compact:NoSchedule`. Also add a fallback label for routing.
Kevin Chen: I suggest nvidia-a10g (a10g) for cost/throughput balance. If we need lower cost, a2-highgpu-1g (smaller) is okay but will increase pod packing complexity.
Anya Patel: Could you paste the commands I should run for quota + subnet checks?
Kevin Chen: Sure — quick checks:
```bash
# check GPU quota in project
gcloud compute regions describe us-west4 --project $P --format="json(quotas)" | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric=="GPUS")'
# check subnet free addresses
gcloud compute networks subnets describe redwood-cluster-subnet --region=us-west4 --project $P --format="json(secondaryIpRanges)"
```
Luca Marino: And our cluster uses secondary range for pods; bumping it requires a rolling plan. If we increase pod secondary range from /22 -> /21 we free ~512 addresses for nodes but need infra change and a short maintenance window.
Ops CI Bot: automated-quota-check: GPUs available: 18, GPUs used: 2, GPUs limit: 20. Subnet free IPs: 28. (run: 1769456799)
SRE-OnCall: If subnet change is painful, alternative is to use smaller node sizes (reduce pods-per-node) or host multiple node pools across subnets and use NodeAffinity to split traffic. Also think about ENI limits for aws-like providers; for GCP we watch vCPU quotas too — GPUs consume vCPU quotas indirectly via instance SKU.
Anya Patel: For autoscaler annotations, do we recommend balance-similar-node-pools? I want short scale-up latency for small requests.
Kevin Chen: Add these on the node pool:
```yaml
nodePool:
  name: compact-gpu
  autoscaling:
    enabled: true
    minNodeCount: 2
    maxNodeCount: 12
  management:
    autoRepair: true
  nodeConfig:
    taints:
      - key: "redwood.com/gpu"
        value: "compact"
        effect: "NO_SCHEDULE"
    labels:
      workload: "compact-infer"
```
Luca Marino: Also set cluster-autoscaler expander to "priority" and enable Pod Priority and Preemption for better packing. Add a small kube-reserved so oom doesn't evict inference.
SRE-OnCall: For canary rollout, create a tiny canary nodepool with 1-2 nodes (reserved) so critical low-QPS requests hit hot nodes and cold starts are avoided. Use autoscaler for burst pool only.
Anya Patel: Okay — plan: create compact-gpu pool with a10g, mixed preemptible= true for 8 spots, 4 guaranteed nodes, taint+label, min=2 max=12. I'll open an infra-PR with subnet bump option if we need.
Kevin Chen: Ping me on the PR; I'll run the quota increase ticket if subnet bump needed. Also run cost estimate: expect ~$0.9–1.2/hr per a10g node on our contract rates (preemptible ~60% cheaper).
Luca Marino: Reminder: update nodepool RBAC to restrict who can schedule on those nodes (node-selector + PSP/PodSecurityDefaults).
Anya Patel: Thanks — I'll draft Terraform snippet and scheduling policy and post here. @SRE-OnCall anything else?
SRE-OnCall: Add a simple alert: if pod pending > 3m with reason "Insufficient GPUs" trigger pager. Also monitor nodepool scale events and set a cooldown to avoid thrashing. :thumbsup:
Anya Patel: Got it, will post PR in ~30m.
Ops CI Bot: terraform-plan: no changes detected for other pools. (run: 1769456840)
